newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse to tighten rules on rogue traders.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse to tighten rules on rogue traders.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) will tighten rules on the business conduct of agents of member brokerage firms to weed out possible rogue traders, an exchange official said on Sunday.

"We think that these revised rules will be crucial for the exchange because...it is possible for one rogue agent to wreck the reputation of the whole exchange," PSE governor Ramon Garcia told reporters.

He said the move by the PSE membership committee to adopt stricter rules was prompted by suspension last week of a broker whom a newspaper columnist had accused of using her account without authority.

Garcia said one proposed regulation would require agents or salesmen to be directly employed by a member-broker. At present, they can transact business through member-brokers without having to be employees.
Garcia said the PSE also planned to ban from the exchange agents who had been terminated by a member-broker for fraudulent acts or for leaving a trail of "troublesome accounts."
Now, all agents will have be licensed by the PSE, he said.
